correctness.rationale: For S=A^(1/2) the derivative solves SX+XS=H and has the stated positive semigroup sandwich integral. Independently, center E_t=e^(−tS) between e^(−vt)I and e^(−ut)I for u=√a, v=√b: the centered rescaled matrix is a spectral contraction, so its absolute row sums are at most √2. Thus the absolute row sum of E_t is bounded by c e^(−ut)+(1−c)e^(−vt), where c=(1+√2)/2. Cauchy–Schwarz on rows or the common row envelope gives the sharp upper bound by the integral of this square. For the positive rank-one low-eigenvalue projection at angle π/8, the first row sum of P is cos²(π/8)+cos(π/8)sin(π/8)=c. Then E_t is entrywise nonnegative and saturates the envelope in that row for all t, and the symmetric all-ones direction gives equality in the (1,1) derivative entry. Integrating gives c²/(2u)+2c(1−c)/(u+v)+(1−c)²/(2v), the stated constant. The scalar-angle derivative in RESULT.md is also obtained by differentiating the row coefficient (1+x)/(1+x²) against its nonnegative kernel. Convex segments give the global bound; admissible interior pairs approach the derivative value and do not assert attainment by distinct matrices. Any finite pair in the unbounded-band domain belongs to some finite band, and the sharp constants tend to the stated unbounded-band value and scalar ratio.
